inputs.title: The Thing
inputs.logline: On his first trip to the Learning Circle, Bo keeps trying to pack away the part of himself he thinks everyone will laugh at, until Keen and Aida help him discover that his poofy tail is the very thing that lets him belong.

orderedEvents.text: Golden morning light. Dew sparkles on wildflowers. A honeycomb sits on a small stump. KEEN tiptoes toward it. He lifts his knees high with every step.
CRUNCH. CRUNCH. CRUNCH.
Keen freezes each time. He spots the honeycomb. His eyes widen. He LICKS HIS LIPS. He reaches toward the honey. FUZZBY the bee is asleep on top of the honeycomb.

orderedEvents.speaker: Fuzzby
orderedEvents.text: ZZZZZ …
A small snore bubble grows from his nose. Keen reaches closer to the honey. POP! The bubble bursts. Keen FREEZES.

orderedEvents.speaker: Fuzzby
orderedEvents.text: ZZZZZ …
Another bubble slowly grows. Keen inches closer to the honey.
POP! The second bubble bursts.

beats.storyBeat: Keen treats the honeycomb like a grand stealth mission, but every crunchy step and Fuzzby’s snore bubbles make his body betray the confidence he is trying to perform. The comedy is suspense built from tiny sounds and over-careful movement.
beats.want: Keen wants to reach the honey without waking Fuzzby.
beats.need: He needs to learn that a failed sneaky plan can still become play rather than defeat.
beats.kidRead: Keen is tiptoeing very badly while a sleepy bee might wake up at any second.
beats.adultRead: A child’s over-serious mission is undone by the ordinary world being louder than his self-image.
beats.emotionalIntent: Warm comic tension: hold the anticipation long enough for the sneeze setup to feel inevitable.

beats.adultRead: The repeated packing is the ache of avoidance made visible without explanation.
beats.emotionalIntent: Quiet wonder with concern underneath; one still, patient mystical breath after the opening comedy.

beats.need: He needs to admit that the delay is not preparation; it is hiding.
beats.kidRead: Bo does not want to go yet, so he talks to his conker and tries to stay home longer.
beats.adultRead: The ordinary parental call lands against the private ritual of a child trying to postpone a hard first day.
beats.emotionalIntent: Domestic warmth tightened by reluctance; funny because the delay logic is so specific and child-real.

direction.premise: Bo is due at the Learning Circle, but the ordinary act of leaving home becomes enormous when his tail keeps doing its embarrassing ‘Thing’; Keen’s playful courage and Aida’s gentle honesty turn that hidden worry into a shared game.
direction.dramaticQuestion: Can Bo take the first step toward a room of new friends before his worry convinces him to stay home?
direction.theme: Belonging begins when the part you are trying to hide is allowed to come with you.
direction.externalJourney: Keen is summoned from a honeycomb prank to collect Bo, help him leave his hollow tree, walk with him through the woods, and arrive at the Learning Circle where the bears welcome Bo’s poofy tail as play rather than a problem.
direction.internalJourney: Bo moves from delaying, repacking and trying to control his tail to letting others see it, play with it, and finally laugh with him instead of at him.
direction.relationshipChanges: Bo begins with only his offscreen mother’s practical nudge, meets Keen as a surprising first friend, receives Aida’s quiet reassurance that brave steps are repeated every time, and ends as part of the group. Keen shifts from mischievous honey-seeker to companion-guide. Aida’s role moves from distant witness to present elder who lends courage without taking the step for Bo.
direction.emotionalCurve: Playful stealth opens the episode, then a calm mystical nudge redirects the story into Bo’s private stop-start worry. The centre deepens through the doorway freeze and tail panic, lifts through Keen’s delighted reframing, dips again on the forest log, steadies through Aida’s shared truth, blossoms through the crystal-lit walk, peaks in communal delight at the Learning Circle, and lands in warm, bittersweet playfulness at sunset.
direction.comedyCurve: The opening runs on snore-bubble suspense and sneeze release; Bo’s packing loop makes worry physically funny; the tail’s repeated POOF becomes a game; Sunny’s over-bright welcome adds group fizz; the final flower-disguise honeycomb reversal pays back the opening with Fuzzby now as the failed sneaker.
direction.setupPayoffMap: The untouched honeycomb and Fuzzby’s ‘never ever’ warning set up the final garden reversal. Keen’s pollen sneeze motivates Aida’s call to him. Aida’s vision of Bo packing and unpacking pays off when she later notices he packed his bag. Bo’s conker and satchel externalise his stop-start leaving. The tail’s first panic POOF becomes a commanded game on the path, then a welcomed performance at the Learning Circle, then a relaxed friendship button with Keen. ‘Every single time’ becomes Bo’s borrowed courage line.
direction.visualMotifs: Round things that hold worry: honeycomb cells, snore bubbles, Bo’s conker, the hollow-tree doorway, the satchel mouth, the poofed tail, cushions in the Learning Circle. Paths and thresholds carry the movement from private worry to shared belonging.
direction.sonicMotifs: Tiny crunches and snore bubbles open as comic tension; Aida’s crystal bowl introduces a warm rose tone; Bo’s POOF becomes a friendly percussion hit; Keen’s sneezes bridge comedy into story; the bear notes gather gently when rose and aquamarine light join on the path.
direction.climax: Aida offers her paw, names through action that going still costs something every time, and Keen adds his Aquamarine call; Bo chooses to walk in the joined pink and blue light, repeating the phrase that has become usable courage.
direction.resolution: At the Learning Circle, Bo’s tail becomes the group’s delight rather than his shame, and later he draws and laughs with Keen while Aida watches with a softly glowing pendant.
direction.intendedFinalFeeling: A warm giggle with a small lump underneath: Bo did not become a different squirrel; he brought the same poofy tail with him and found it welcomed.

northStar.surfaceStory: In the Crystal Clearing, Aida’s bowl tone reveals a rose-lit glimpse of Bo repeatedly trying and failing to finish packing for the Learning Circle; then Keen’s off-camera sneezes puncture the hush, and Aida calls him to come with her.
northStar.universalTruth: Sometimes the person who can help is not the perfectly calm grown-up, but the messy friend whose silliness makes the scary doorway feel playable.
northStar.childClearWant: Aida wants to find who needs help and bring Keen with her.
northStar.emotionalNeed: Aida needs to recognise that Bo’s stuckness may need companionship and play, not a solemn fix.
northStar.falseBeliefUnderPressure: If someone is struggling, the safest help is quiet, careful, grown-up control.
northStar.relationshipEngine: Aida’s stillness meets Keen’s chaotic sneezy honesty: his ridiculous interruption changes the rescue from mystical diagnosis into warm, practical togetherness.
northStar.ordinaryLifeTruth: A child frozen before a new place often does not need a lecture about bravery; they need someone beside them who makes the next step feel less heavy.
northStar.sceneTurn: The off-camera sneeze breaks the sacred rose-lit vision and reveals the episode’s help will travel through Keen’s imperfect, honey-scented mischief rather than Aida’s stillness alone.
audienceJourney: Hushed curiosity as the bowl tone opens the vision.
Tender recognition when Bo’s stop-start packing shows he cannot cross the threshold.
Comic release when Keen’s sneeze crashes into the quiet.
Warm anticipation as Aida folds the joke into purpose and invites Keen along.
northStar.finalAfterFeeling: The scene should leave us smiling and leaning forward: Bo is not fixed yet, but help is already becoming friend-shaped.
northStar.dialogueSubtractionOpportunity: Do not add any spoken explanation of Bo being nervous, embarrassed, or afraid. His repeated packing, the rose haze, and Aida’s held look carry that. Also avoid adding any line that explains why Keen is useful; the sneeze, honeycomb reference, and Aida’s choice to call him in make the point.
northStar.environmentPressure: The Crystal Clearing begins as a held, ritual space where every small sound matters; the bowl tone and rose vision demand stillness, so Keen’s sneeze physically and emotionally invades the calm, forcing Aida to shift from contemplation into action.

inputs.logline: On his first trip to the Learning Circle, Bo keeps trying to pack away the part of himself he thinks everyone will laugh at, until Keen and Aida help him discover that his poofy tail is the very thing that lets him belong.

orderedEvents.text: Golden morning light. Dew sparkles on wildflowers. A honeycomb sits on a small stump. KEEN tiptoes toward it. He lifts his knees high with every step.
CRUNCH. CRUNCH. CRUNCH.
Keen freezes each time. He spots the honeycomb. His eyes widen. He LICKS HIS LIPS. He reaches toward the honey. FUZZBY the bee is asleep on top of the honeycomb.

orderedEvents.speaker: Fuzzby
orderedEvents.text: ZZZZZ …
A small snore bubble grows from his nose. Keen reaches closer to the honey. POP! The bubble bursts. Keen FREEZES.

orderedEvents.speaker: Fuzzby
orderedEvents.text: ZZZZZ …
Another bubble slowly grows. Keen inches closer to the honey.
POP! The second bubble bursts.

beats.storyBeat: Keen treats the honeycomb like a grand stealth mission, but every crunchy step and Fuzzby’s snore bubbles make his body betray the confidence he is trying to perform. The comedy is suspense built from tiny sounds and over-careful movement.
beats.want: Keen wants to reach the honey without waking Fuzzby.
beats.need: He needs to learn that a failed sneaky plan can still become play rather than defeat.
beats.kidRead: Keen is tiptoeing very badly while a sleepy bee might wake up at any second.
beats.adultRead: A child’s over-serious mission is undone by the ordinary world being louder than his self-image.
beats.emotionalIntent: Warm comic tension: hold the anticipation long enough for the sneeze setup to feel inevitable.

treatments.name: The Sacred Circle Gets Sneezed Open
treatments.audienceExperience: The audience begins in a hush, almost holding its breath with Aida. The rose-lit vision feels fragile and important, then Keen’s sneeze detonates the quiet in a way that makes children laugh and adults recognise the mercy of imperfection arriving at exactly the right time. The scene leaves us feeling that Aida’s calm has not been ruined; it has been widened.
treatments.emotionalPointOfView: Aida owns the scene. We experience her careful attention to Bo’s stuckness first, then her quiet adjustment when the world refuses to stay ceremonial. Her want is to understand who needs help; her need is to allow the help to become playful rather than perfectly controlled.
treatments.comicOrDramaticMechanism: The dramatic mechanism is stillness invaded by bodily comedy. The comic mechanism is silence replacing dialogue, then environmental/sound interruption: Aida’s solemn bowl tone creates a sacred rule, and Keen’s off-camera sneeze breaks it with such sincerity that the break becomes the solution. The sneeze is not random noise; it is the doorway from mystical noticing into friend-shaped action.
treatments.characterPerformanceStrategy: Aida moves very little. Her performance lives in a slow breath, a settled hand near the bowl, eyes softening when Bo’s repeated packing appears, and the smallest adjustment of her attention when the sneeze lands. She does not snap out of the vision; she absorbs the interruption. Keen is heard before seen or summoned: his sneezes must feel full-bodied, helpless, and honey-scented in their comic implication. Bo, inside the vision, is all stop-start behaviour: pack, hesitate, almost commit, undo or stall — never a labelled feeling.
treatments.visualGrammar: The scene begins as a contained ritual: circular shapes, gentle verticals, warm morning clarity drawn into a rose-pink field. The rose vision fills the frame when active; we do not treat it as a small object in a wider room. When the sneeze breaks in, the frame’s order loosens: not chaotic, but airier, as if the clearing has remembered the outside world exists.
treatments.cameraCharacterRelationship: The camera sits with Aida’s attention rather than observing her from a safe distance. It discovers Bo through her bowl tone, entering the rose haze as if drawn by sound. When Keen sneezes off-camera, the camera does not instantly explain him; it lets Aida’s reaction tell us the interruption matters before the world opens toward his direction.
treatments.movementVersusStillness: Stillness has value here only because it is under pressure. Aida and the bowl are held, grounded, and nearly unmoving; Bo’s small repeated packing gives the inner movement; Keen’s sneeze is off-screen kinetic force. The scene’s turn is the moment Aida chooses not to restore stillness, but to convert it into forward motion: “Keen? Come with me.”
treatments.depthAndEnvironment: The Crystal Clearing begins as a safe, shallow-feeling circle around Aida and the bowl, with dew and morning texture present but subdued. In the vision, depth compresses around Bo’s threshold behaviour so his repeated packing feels private and close. After the sneeze, depth returns: the clearing has edges again, and Keen exists somewhere beyond them, noisy and useful.
treatments.rhythmAndEscalation: The rhythm starts slow: bowl tone, rose haze, Bo’s repeated unfinished action. Aida’s line lands as a quiet naming of need. Then the sneeze interrupts with comic over-size. The second Aida line folds the disruption into purpose, and Keen’s answering sneeze gives one last burst of comedy before Aida’s final blessing settles the scene warmly.
treatments.cutPhilosophy: Cuts are motivated by changed state: ordinary clearing to full-frame vision; Bo’s repeated threshold struggle to Aida’s recognition; recognition to sneeze rupture; rupture to invitation. Avoid automatic reaction coverage. Aida’s held look earns more than a cut if her thought is still changing; cut only when new information, comic punctuation, or a changed point of view arrives.
treatments.openingImage: A calm bowl at the centre of morning warmth, rose light beginning to gather as Aida’s still hands make the clearing feel safe enough to listen.
treatments.closingImage: Aida’s still centre now angled outward toward the noisy edge of the clearing, having invited Keen into the mission; the rose hush has become warm movement.
treatments.cinematographerChallenge: Do not make this a polite medium shot of Aida looking into a magic object. The risk is reverence becoming static. The camera must make the bowl tone feel like it pulls us into Bo’s private hesitation, then make the sneeze physically disturb the frame’s sense of order without resorting to frantic movement or gag coverage.

treatments.name: Inside the Rose Haze, the Outside World Knocks
treatments.audienceExperience: The audience is placed almost entirely inside the rose-lit vision at first, watching Bo’s tiny unfinished packing attempts as if we have been trusted with a secret. The sneeze then arrives from a world we had nearly forgotten, popping the emotional bubble. Children get the funny shock; adults feel how a solemn adult gaze can become too heavy until a silly friend gives the moment oxygen.
treatments.emotionalPointOfView: The emotional point of view is Bo’s stuck threshold as perceived by Aida. We do not enter Bo’s thoughts verbally; we enter the pattern of his body. Aida is the reader of the image, but the audience’s tenderness is generated by being trapped for a while in Bo’s repeated almost-going.
treatments.comicOrDramaticMechanism: The dramatic mechanism is private repetition: the same small packing action failing to complete until it becomes unmistakable. The comic mechanism is anticipation to reversal: the rose haze promises a grand mystical answer, but the answer is punctured by Keen’s gigantic sneeze and Aida’s dry-warm deduction about Fuzzby’s honeycomb.
treatments.characterPerformanceStrategy: Bo’s performance is precise and small: paws deciding, pausing, restarting; a pack that becomes a threshold rather than a prop. No exaggerated trembling, no explanatory face. Aida’s performance is receptive: she watches without leaning in to fix. Keen’s voice is the comic body off-screen — sneeze first, personality second — and his “Coming, Aida!” should sound eager even while his nose is still winning.
treatments.visualGrammar: The vision is not an effect layered over the scene; it temporarily becomes the scene. Rose haze at the margins, softened contrast, sound-led entry. Bo’s packing is framed as a loop with slight variations, so each restart carries more feeling. The sneeze breaks the haze back to ordinary morning colour, not as a failure of magic but as a return to playable life.
treatments.cameraCharacterRelationship: The camera is invited into Aida’s seeing, then held inside Bo’s private space longer than expected. It should not keep reassuring us where Aida is during the vision. Once Keen sneezes, the camera’s relationship changes: it remembers Aida’s body in the clearing and lets her choose what the interruption means.
treatments.movementVersusStillness: Movement is tiny inside the vision and huge outside it. Bo’s small motions become monumental because the frame attends to them. Aida’s stillness surrounds the vision. Keen’s sneeze is movement without image at first — an off-screen force that makes the scene breathe again.
treatments.depthAndEnvironment: Inside the rose haze, environment is threshold and pack: enough world to know Bo is preparing to leave, not enough to distract from his inability to complete the action. The Crystal Clearing returns after the sneeze with morning space, dew, and air, making the contrast between inner stuckness and outer possibility clear.
treatments.rhythmAndEscalation: Begin with sustained tone and gentle duration. Let Bo’s repetition accumulate: first curious, then tender, then unmistakably stuck. Aida’s “Someone needs a little help today” lands as recognition, not diagnosis. The sneeze interrupts before the scene can become too solemn, and the final exchange accelerates into practical action.
treatments.cutPhilosophy: Use fewer cuts during the vision so the audience feels the repetition rather than being told to notice it. The key cut is the rupture back to Aida and ordinary morning after Keen’s sneeze. Subsequent cuts, if any, should be comic punctuation and orientation toward the off-screen Keen, not standard dialogue alternation.
treatments.openingImage: Rose haze filling the frame around Bo’s half-finished pack, his paws caught in the almost of leaving.
treatments.closingImage: The haze gone, Aida in morning clarity calling toward an unseen sneezy friend, the private worry now connected to outside companionship.
treatments.cinematographerChallenge: Do not over-protect the audience with a conventional establishing view of Aida, bowl, and vision all at once. The bolder choice is to let the vision occupy us completely, trusting sound and Aida’s later reaction to restore geography. The danger is making Bo’s struggle decorative; the camera must make repetition feel like pressure.

treatments.name: Aida’s Quiet Centre, Keen’s Noisy Orbit
treatments.audienceExperience: The audience watches a quiet centre surrounded by a world that cannot help being alive. The bowl tone and rose vision make Aida feel like the clearing’s steady heart; Keen’s off-camera sneezes are the messy orbit crashing in from the edge. The pleasure is seeing Aida’s wisdom include the mess rather than correct it.
treatments.emotionalPointOfView: This version is governed by the relationship engine between Aida and unseen Keen. Bo’s need is the tender discovery, but the scene’s transformation is Aida realising that the helper should not be only the calmest presence in the clearing. Her stillness remains powerful, but it becomes porous.
treatments.comicOrDramaticMechanism: The mechanism is contrast in one scene-shape: composed ritual versus off-screen bodily chaos. The joke is not that Keen is wrong to interrupt; the joke is that his interruption is so perfectly timed it becomes useful. Aida’s “Bless you” and honeycomb deduction turn the sneeze from nuisance into character evidence.
treatments.characterPerformanceStrategy: Aida’s first line is low, warm, and certain, as if spoken to the clearing as much as to herself. On the sneeze, she should not startle broadly; a tiny blink, a slight turn of the head, and a patient acceptance are funnier and truer. Keen’s sneezes must have escalating helplessness: the first rupture, the second confirming this is not over, the final one attached to his enthusiastic obedience. Bo remains glimpsed through action, not interpreted.
treatments.visualGrammar: The frame treats Aida as a quiet gravitational centre, with the clearing’s edges alive in sound and implied movement. The rose vision is central but not isolating in spirit: it is Aida’s way of listening. When Keen enters sonically, composition opens toward negative space at the edge, making absence funny — the noisy character we cannot yet see has already changed the scene.
treatments.cameraCharacterRelationship: The camera respects Aida’s stillness but is not frozen by it. It may begin close to the bowl’s sound, drift into the rose vision, then return to Aida with enough off-screen space for Keen’s sneeze to invade. It does not chase Keen immediately; it lets him be an acoustic character until Aida summons him.
treatments.movementVersusStillness: Aida’s stillness is the anchor. Bo’s packing is small repeated movement within her attention. Keen’s movement is imagined through sound: sneezes that seem to travel from beyond the frame. The final movement is directional rather than physical spectacle — Aida’s attention turns outward, and the scene’s purpose starts moving.
treatments.depthAndEnvironment: Use the clearing as a listening space. Morning dew and wild detail should make tiny sounds plausible and precious before the sneeze overwhelms them. After the interruption, the off-screen edge matters: Keen is not in the sacred centre yet, but the centre has extended to include him.
treatments.rhythmAndEscalation: The scene plays as hush, recognition, rupture, incorporation, launch. Let the bowl tone hold long enough that the sneeze feels like it has broken a rule. Then avoid overplaying delay; Aida’s warmth quickly metabolises the interruption. Keen’s final sneeze after “Coming, Aida!” is the button that keeps the mission playful.
treatments.cutPhilosophy: Cuts should behave like attention, not coverage. Stay with Aida when her thought is the event. Enter the vision when the bowl tone creates new information. Cut or reframe on the sneeze only if it changes the room’s emotional balance. Do not cut to Keen merely because he speaks off-camera; withholding him keeps the comic mechanism alive.
treatments.openingImage: Aida and the bowl held in morning quiet, with rose light beginning to pulse from the centre while the clearing seems to listen.
treatments.closingImage: Aida turned toward the unseen sneezy edge, her calm intact but opened outward, the mission now shared with the very mess that interrupted it.
treatments.cinematographerChallenge: The safe version would be a centred mentor shot with magical insert and off-screen audio. Reject that. The frame must give off-screen space dramatic weight: Keen’s absence should be visible as charged empty air. The challenge is making a character who is not yet seen alter composition, rhythm, and emotional meaning.

treatmentSelection.selectedTreatment: Combined treatment: “The Rose Secret Gets Sneezed Open”
combinedFrom: Inside the Rose Haze, the Outside World Knocks
Aida’s Quiet Centre, Keen’s Noisy Orbit
The Sacred Circle Gets Sneezed Open
treatmentSelection.governingAudienceExperience: The audience is trusted inside Bo’s private almost-ready feeling, held in Aida’s sacred hush, then released into laughter when Keen’s unseen sneezy mess makes the help feel playable instead of solemn.
treatmentSelection.rationale: Select a combination, led by the boldness of “Inside the Rose Haze” and emotionally governed by “Aida’s Quiet Centre.” The scene should not politely watch Aida watching a vision; it should let the rose haze temporarily become the scene so Bo’s repeated half-packing feels like pressure, not information. That gives the child audience a clear visual game — he keeps almost doing it — while adults feel the ache of a child stuck at a threshold. But Aida must remain the transforming owner, so we take “Quiet Centre” as the spine: her stillness is not broken by Keen’s interruption, it becomes porous. Keen stays off-screen long enough to be a comic force, not a cutaway obligation. The final turn is Aida choosing to include the mess, which makes the episode’s help friend-shaped. “Sacred Circle” contributes the correct rhythm and tone: hush, rose-lit recognition, sneeze rupture, warm incorporation, launch. The winning approach commits to contrast inside one emotional event: tiny private repetition versus enormous off-screen sneeze; ritual stillness versus sticky real-life play; mystical noticing versus practical companionship.
treatmentSelection.rejectionChecks: No submitted treatment is rejected for depending on fixed character lanes, keeping all characters visible, habitual action/reaction coverage, safe camera placement, repeated close-up punctuation, mechanical shot counts, generic cinematic language, or mere script illustration. The selected combination explicitly avoids those traps: Aida is not kept visible during the whole vision; Keen is withheld off-screen; cuts follow changed emotional state rather than dialogue alternation; the camera is pulled by bowl tone and sneeze disturbance rather than parked safely. Full literal adoption of “The Sacred Circle Gets Sneezed Open” is not preferred because it could become too balanced and reverent if staged as Aida plus magic insert. Full literal adoption of “Inside the Rose Haze” is not preferred because it risks making Bo’s private stuckness the whole ownership of the scene unless Aida’s changed relationship to Keen’s mess remains decisive. Full literal adoption of “Aida’s Quiet Centre” is not preferred because its centre/orbit idea needs the rose-haze immersion from Treatment 2 to keep Bo’s threshold behaviour emotionally unmistakable.

orderedEvents.text: Soft mist floats through tall trees. AIDA sits beside a crystal bowl. She slowly circles a mallet around the rim. A warm tone hums through the clearing. Her ROSE QUARTZ PENDANT begins to glow. Pink light fills her eyes.
VISION – THROUGH AIDA'S EYES
A small red squirrel sits inside a hollow tree. He packs a satchel. Unpacks it. Packs it again. He doesn't move. BACK TO SCENE. Aida gently stops the bowl. She places a paw on her heart.

beats.whatChanges: The clearing’s ordinary morning quiet becomes a rose-lit field of attention, and Bo’s private stop-start packing changes from unseen offscreen life into the scene’s central need.
beats.whoDrives: Aida drives the change by holding still, sounding the bowl, and staying with what the vision shows instead of rushing to interpret it aloud.
beats.audienceAnticipation: The audience leans into the hush, expecting the bowl tone to reveal who needs help and what kind of trouble the day is asking Aida to notice.
beats.actionOrChoice: Aida lets the bowl tone pull the scene into the rose haze; within it, Bo repeatedly packs, hesitates, almost commits, then stalls or undoes the motion. Aida chooses to read the repetition gently, without naming the feeling or turning it into a lesson.
beats.consequence: Bo’s threshold behaviour becomes tenderly unmistakable: he wants to go, but cannot yet cross. The rose haze makes the struggle feel close, private, and fragile rather than like information in a magic object.
beats.emotionalOrComicHandover: The beat hands over a sacred hush with pressure inside it: the audience understands that someone needs help before the scene allows any comic release.

shots.purpose: Open Aida’s sacred attention and reveal Bo’s private threshold struggle through the bowl vision.
shots.audienceExperience: The audience is trusted into a fragile hush, then into Bo’s repeated almost-going rhythm before Aida quietly receives what it means.
shots.openingImage: A crystal bowl rests in the morning clearing between Aida’s still hands as faint rose light begins to collect along its rim.
shots.principalPerformance: Aida moves very little: the mallet’s slow circle, a quiet breath, softened eyes, then the small paw-to-heart recognition after the vision releases.
shots.cameraRelationship: The camera sits inside Aida’s act of listening; it is drawn by the bowl tone into the rose field and returns only when the vision’s evidence has accumulated.

direction.premise: Bo is due at the Learning Circle, but the ordinary act of leaving home becomes enormous when his tail keeps doing its embarrassing ‘Thing’; Keen’s playful courage and Aida’s gentle honesty turn that hidden worry into a shared game.
direction.dramaticQuestion: Can Bo take the first step toward a room of new friends before his worry convinces him to stay home?
direction.theme: Belonging begins when the part you are trying to hide is allowed to come with you.
direction.externalJourney: Keen is summoned from a honeycomb prank to collect Bo, help him leave his hollow tree, walk with him through the woods, and arrive at the Learning Circle where the bears welcome Bo’s poofy tail as play rather than a problem.
direction.internalJourney: Bo moves from delaying, repacking and trying to control his tail to letting others see it, play with it, and finally laugh with him instead of at him.
direction.relationshipChanges: Bo begins with only his offscreen mother’s practical nudge, meets Keen as a surprising first friend, receives Aida’s quiet reassurance that brave steps are repeated every time, and ends as part of the group. Keen shifts from mischievous honey-seeker to companion-guide. Aida’s role moves from distant witness to present elder who lends courage without taking the step for Bo.
direction.emotionalCurve: Playful stealth opens the episode, then a calm mystical nudge redirects the story into Bo’s private stop-start worry. The centre deepens through the doorway freeze and tail panic, lifts through Keen’s delighted reframing, dips again on the forest log, steadies through Aida’s shared truth, blossoms through the crystal-lit walk, peaks in communal delight at the Learning Circle, and lands in warm, bittersweet playfulness at sunset.
direction.comedyCurve: The opening runs on snore-bubble suspense and sneeze release; Bo’s packing loop makes worry physically funny; the tail’s repeated POOF becomes a game; Sunny’s over-bright welcome adds group fizz; the final flower-disguise honeycomb reversal pays back the opening with Fuzzby now as the failed sneaker.
direction.setupPayoffMap: The untouched honeycomb and Fuzzby’s ‘never ever’ warning set up the final garden reversal. Keen’s pollen sneeze motivates Aida’s call to him. Aida’s vision of Bo packing and unpacking pays off when she later notices he packed his bag. Bo’s conker and satchel externalise his stop-start leaving. The tail’s first panic POOF becomes a commanded game on the path, then a welcomed performance at the Learning Circle, then a relaxed friendship button with Keen. ‘Every single time’ becomes Bo’s borrowed courage line.
direction.visualMotifs: Round things that hold worry: honeycomb cells, snore bubbles, Bo’s conker, the hollow-tree doorway, the satchel mouth, the poofed tail, cushions in the Learning Circle. Paths and thresholds carry the movement from private worry to shared belonging.
direction.sonicMotifs: Tiny crunches and snore bubbles open as comic tension; Aida’s crystal bowl introduces a warm rose tone; Bo’s POOF becomes a friendly percussion hit; Keen’s sneezes bridge comedy into story; the bear notes gather gently when rose and aquamarine light join on the path.
direction.climax: Aida offers her paw, names through action that going still costs something every time, and Keen adds his Aquamarine call; Bo chooses to walk in the joined pink and blue light, repeating the phrase that has become usable courage.
direction.resolution: At the Learning Circle, Bo’s tail becomes the group’s delight rather than his shame, and later he draws and laughs with Keen while Aida watches with a softly glowing pendant.
direction.intendedFinalFeeling: A warm giggle with a small lump underneath: Bo did not become a different squirrel; he brought the same poofy tail with him and found it welcomed.

scenePurposeAndEmotionalChange.dramaticQuestion: Will Aida treat Bo’s stuckness as something to solve through perfect stillness, or recognise that messy friendship may be the doorway he needs?

dramaticBeats.beginning: The clearing’s ordinary morning quiet becomes a rose-lit field of attention, and Bo’s private stop-start packing changes from unseen offscreen life into the scene’s central need.
dramaticBeats.development: The rose hush opens back into ordinary morning space. Keen remains comic and unseen long enough to feel like a force from the edge of the clearing, and Aida’s calm widens into forward motion.
dramaticBeats.turn: Aida speaks the need, absorbs the off-camera sneeze without snapping out of herself, lightly connects it to honeycomb mischief, blesses Keen, and calls him to come with her. Keen answers from off-camera and sneezes again.
dramaticBeats.landing: The beat hands over warm comic momentum: Bo is not fixed, but the rescue has become less heavy because Aida has invited the imperfect friend into it.

performanceDirection.principalPerformance: Aida moves very little: the mallet’s slow circle, a quiet breath, softened eyes, then the small paw-to-heart recognition after the vision releases.
performanceDirection.physicalPerformance: Aida’s body stays rooted beside the bowl, with only the slow mallet circle, a quiet breath, and softened eyes carrying the ritual. Inside the rose field, Bo’s paws repeat the satchel task in a stop-start rhythm: commitment gathers, stalls, reverses, then gathers again without his feet crossing the hollow-tree threshold. On return, Aida lets the bowl quiet and brings one paw to her heart, receiving the vision without extra motion.

contract.playableIntention: Aida is not trying to command an answer; she is making the clearing safe enough for the need to show itself. Bo is caught in an almost-ready loop that his hands reveal before any explanation could.

phases.observableAction: Aida sits grounded at bowl height and circles the mallet around the rim with an even, restrained hand as rose light gathers along the bowl and in her eyes.
Bo packs the satchel, stops before leaving the hollow-tree opening, unpacks it, then packs it again while remaining inside the threshold.
Aida gently stops the bowl, lets her gaze soften after the vision releases, and places one paw against her heart.
The full-frame rose haze thins back into warm morning air while the bowl surface and surrounding mist become still.

contract.physicalCauseAndEffect: Aida’s steady mallet pressure keeps the bowl vibrating; the vibration draws rose light into the frame and opens the vision. Bo’s repeated handling changes the satchel’s state without changing his position, making the unstepped doorway the visible obstacle. When Aida removes the mallet’s motion, the tone and rose field subside, leaving her paw-to-heart gesture as the physical receipt of what she has seen.
contract.visibleEmotionalTurn: The shot changes from ceremonial listening to tender recognition: Aida’s eyes move from searching focus to softened concern, and Bo’s repeated packing becomes the evidence she holds.
contract.requiredLanding: End on Aida beside the quiet bowl with one paw at her heart, rose glow fading into morning warmth, clearly understanding that Bo is stuck at a threshold without having fixed it.
contract.performanceFreedom: Keep the exact cadence of Bo’s pauses, Aida’s breath, robe follow-through, and rose-haze dissipation flexible, as long as the actions remain restrained, readable, and never rushed.

characterTruths.canonTrait: Aida is the warm, still elder anchor whose confidence shows as grounded self-knowledge, not display.
characterTruths.playableWant: She wants the bowl ritual to reveal who needs care and to hold that discovery safely.
characterTruths.pressureResponse: Under the pressure of another’s private need, she becomes quieter and more still rather than busier.
characterTruths.observableSignature: Settled posture, minimal hand motion, softened eyes, and a gentle paw-to-heart gesture after the bowl stops.
characterTruths.substitutionTest: Another character could make the vision feel like magic or investigation; only Aida’s stillness makes the reveal feel like a safe space that holds Bo without fixing him.

characterTruths.canonTrait: Supplied scene canon defines Bo here by private stop-start threshold behaviour: he wants to go but cannot yet cross out of the hollow tree.
characterTruths.playableWant: He wants the satchel to be ready enough for him to leave.
characterTruths.pressureResponse: Under the pressure of leaving, his paws restart the task while his body stays inside the doorway.
characterTruths.observableSignature: Pack, halt, unpack, repack, with no step past the hollow-tree threshold.
characterTruths.substitutionTest: A more outward or verbal character would turn the moment into explanation or a joke; Bo’s function here is the quiet, repeated almost-action that Aida can witness.

performanceDirection.principalPerformance: Aida’s decisive action is restraint plus reorientation: she does not restart the bowl or reclaim the ritual; she lets her attention and body open toward Keen’s noisy direction.
performanceDirection.physicalPerformance: Aida begins settled beside the inactive bowl, carrying the vision’s residue in her stillness. Keen’s off-camera sneezes enter as full-body force before he is fully explained: dew trembles, air loosens, and later he brushes at his nose while recovering across the clearing. Aida registers the interruption with eyes and breath first, then leaves the bowl alone and turns her posture outward. Keen’s approach stays eager but sneeze-disrupted; Aida remains grounded as the opened path becomes the final read.

contract.playableIntention: Aida decides the interruption belongs inside the help rather than outside it. Keen is trying to answer and join, but his body keeps turning eagerness into comic interruption.

phases.observableAction: Aida sits beside the quiet bowl with her body still and her attention lifted from the vision, holding the ritual space closed for one last beat.
Keen erupts from off-camera with oversized sneezes that make nearby dew, light texture, and settled air shiver before his body is clearly identified.
Aida’s eyes and breath shift toward the sound; she does not flinch broadly, reach for the bowl, or restart the ritual.
Aida turns her body and eyeline outward toward Keen’s direction, leaving the bowl inactive as the clearing edge becomes part of the mission.

contract.physicalCauseAndEffect: The quiet bowl space creates still air; Keen’s off-camera sneeze sends a visible ripple through dew and light texture. Aida’s body absorbs the disturbance without recoiling, and because she does not return her hand to the bowl, the ritual remains open. Her outward turn redirects the scene’s energy from closed ceremony toward shared movement.
contract.visibleEmotionalTurn: The shot changes from protected solemnity to widened calm: Aida’s attention shifts from the bowl’s centre to Keen’s noisy direction, and the interruption becomes included rather than corrected.
contract.requiredLanding: End with Aida grounded beside the bowl, turned toward the active clearing edge, with Keen established as the messy approaching companion and the path outward visually open.
contract.performanceFreedom: Keen’s sneeze recovery, nose-brushing, jog rhythm, and secondary body recoil may vary for comic life; Aida’s micro-pause, breath, and robe follow-through may breathe, provided she never becomes frantic or scolding.

characterTruths.canonTrait: Aida leads through warm grounded stillness; she makes space feel safe and does not rush, preach, or control by force.
characterTruths.playableWant: She wants to turn what she has witnessed into the right kind of help without breaking the safety of the moment.
characterTruths.pressureResponse: When bodily comedy invades the fragile hush, she grows more spacious instead of tighter, choosing to include the interruption.
characterTruths.observableSignature: Small eye shift, contained breath, hands staying away from the bowl, and a slow outward turn that opens the circle.
characterTruths.substitutionTest: A more reactive character would chase the noise, scold it, or make the gag the whole point; only Aida can make the sneeze feel welcomed into a caring mission.

characterTruths.canonTrait: Supplied canon places Keen as the eager young bear Aida once welcomed into belonging; in this beat he is messy, sincere, and useful precisely because he cannot stay polished.
characterTruths.playableWant: He wants to respond and come join Aida despite his sneeze-disrupted body.
characterTruths.pressureResponse: Under the pressure of being called in while recovering, his eagerness pushes forward but his sneezes keep interrupting his control.
characterTruths.observableSignature: Off-camera full-body sneeze force, pollen-brushing recovery, eager approach, and another sneeze overtaking the movement.
characterTruths.substitutionTest: Another character might make the interruption clever, deliberate, or neat; Keen’s specific value is sincere, helpless eagerness that breaks the hush without meanness.

comedyStaging.staysVisible: Aida and the disturbed ritual space stay visible at the sneeze’s first impact; Keen remains off-camera so the sound acts like a comic force entering the frame.
comedyStaging.contactAndWeight: The sneeze should read as full-bodied force through the environment: a slight tremble in dew, a tiny shiver in the bowl’s settled surface or nearby light texture, and Aida’s robes responding only subtly because she remains grounded.

performances.speaker: Aida
performances.exactDialogue: 7	Someone needs a little help today. (AIDA reacts to off camera SNEEZE)
performances.voiceIdentity: Aida: grounded, warm, ritual-still; voice stays close and steady, with humor arriving as a soft recognition rather than a punchline.
performances.dramaticIntention: Aida wants to gently reorient herself from the vision toward whoever is in need, without breaking the calm she has just received.
performances.subtext: The bowl has shown her someone struggling; the sneeze confirms it. She is amused, but also quietly ready to help.
performances.relationshipTarget: Primarily to herself and the opened clearing; secondarily toward the unseen sneezer, as if making room for them before naming them.
performances.emotionalEntry: Still carrying the rose-field vision, inward and softened, paw-to-heart residue present.
performances.emotionalExit: Warmly attentive; the ritual is released and her focus opens outward.
performances.pace: Slow-to-medium; let the first thought arrive after the sneeze impact, then finish with calm certainty.
performances.rhythm: One gentle recognition arc: observe, understand, accept.
performances.pauses: Protect a small pause after the off-camera sneeze before speaking. Tiny settling pause after “Someone” so the thought can turn from mystery to care.
performances.breaths: Quiet nasal breath before the line; no dramatic gasp. Breath should feel like Aida letting the bowl go.
performances.nonVerbalActions: Eyes lift first, then a small breath; body remains rooted beside the inactive bowl. No restart of the mallet, no fussing.
performances.elevenLabsV3Direction: ElevenLabs text, excluding script number and parenthetical: [quietly] Someone needs a little help today. Start after the sneeze lands and the dew tremble has had a beat. Put mild warmth on “Someone,” gentler purpose on “help,” and let “today” settle like a decision, not a joke.
performances.physicalActionRelationship: Voice supports the restraint: the line is the sound of Aida turning her attention outward while the body barely moves.
performances.expectedTiming: Begin roughly 0.5–0.8s after the sneeze impact; line lasts about 2.0s, with a soft hold after.

performances.speaker: Keen
performances.voiceIdentity: Keen: eager, open-hearted, physically impulsive; even a sneeze has forward momentum and too much commitment.
performances.dramaticIntention: Keen’s body wants to keep arriving and being useful, but the sneeze hijacks the whole performance.
performances.subtext: He is trying to be fine and on his way, but his nose is absolutely in charge.
performances.relationshipTarget: Off-camera Aida and the clearing he is crashing into; the sneeze announces him before he can properly announce himself.
performances.emotionalEntry: Eager approach, disrupted by a building tickle he cannot control.
performances.emotionalExit: More exposed and comic; he has accidentally made himself the center of attention.
performances.pace: Broad and explosive, with a brief recoil/reset between sneezes.
performances.rhythm: Two full-body blasts: wind-up, release; shorter recovery; second wind-up, bigger release.
performances.pauses: A clear comic beat between the two sneezes so dew/air reaction can register.
performances.breaths: Audible involuntary inhale before each sneeze; the second inhale should sound like he knows it is coming and cannot stop it.
performances.nonVerbalActions: The sneeze force travels through the clearing before Keen is fully explained: dew trembles, air loosens, his body gets knocked off its eager rhythm.
performances.elevenLabsV3Direction: ElevenLabs text: [gasps] AHHHHCHHOOOOO!!! [pause] [gasps] AHHHHCHHOOOOO!!! Make both sneezes big and physical, not scary; the second one can be slightly more helpless and funny. Keep it child-safe and plush, never harsh or painful.
performances.physicalActionRelationship: Voice drives the broad physical interruption: the sound should feel strong enough to disturb dew and knock Keen’s approach off-beat.
performances.expectedTiming: First sneeze hits as the interruption; hold about 0.4–0.6s for environmental reaction, then the second sneeze lands broader.

performances.voiceIdentity: Aida: calm caretaker with a dry little sparkle; never scolds, never rushes, lets the joke sit inside kindness.
performances.dramaticIntention: Aida wants Keen to feel seen, gently teased, and safely gathered toward help.
performances.subtext: I know exactly what happened, and you are not in trouble; come here before your nose takes over the whole clearing.
performances.relationshipTarget: Keen, off to the side or approaching through the clearing; Aida’s voice opens a path for him.
performances.emotionalEntry: Warmly attentive after the sneeze impacts, still grounded beside the inactive bowl.
performances.emotionalExit: Purposeful and inviting; she has fully chosen Keen’s need over continuing the ritual.
performances.pace: Unhurried, conversational; the tease gets a tiny lift, then the invitation becomes practical and kind.
performances.rhythm: Blessing; amused deduction; name as a soft check-in; invitation as gentle leadership.
performances.pauses: Small pause after “Bless you.” Let “Sounds like…” enter with a knowing smile. Pause after “Keen?” to allow him to be found in the space before the invitation.
performances.breaths: One quiet breath before “Sounds,” as if Aida is letting amusement pass through without making it too big.
performances.nonVerbalActions: Aida leaves the bowl inactive, turns posture outward, and uses only eyes/breath before the fuller orientation. No extra hand business.

performances.physicalActionRelationship: Voice mirrors the body’s reorientation: restrained warmth at first, then opening outward as she chooses the path toward Keen.
performances.expectedTiming: Begin after the second sneeze’s broad impact has cleared. Total line about 5.0–6.0s, with the biggest held space after “Keen?”

performances.speaker: Keen
performances.voiceIdentity: Keen: bright, eager-to-please, a little overpowered by his own body; tries to sound capable right up until the sneeze wins.
performances.dramaticIntention: Keen wants Aida to know he is responding immediately and is totally fine, even as the sneeze proves otherwise.
performances.subtext: I’m coming! I’ve got this! I absolutely do not got this.
performances.relationshipTarget: Aida, across the clearing; he is answering her call while still physically recovering.
performances.emotionalEntry: Relieved to be invited, trying to recover dignity and momentum.
performances.emotionalExit: Comic helplessness; his eagerness survives, but his nose has undercut him again.

performances.rhythm: Bright response, tiny tickle warning, then involuntary blast.
performances.pauses: No formal pause after “Aida!”; instead a caught micro-beat where the sneeze overtakes him.
performances.breaths: Quick eager breath into “Coming”; sharp involuntary inhale before the sneeze.
performances.nonVerbalActions: Keen brushes at his nose or fights the tickle while still moving toward Aida; the sneeze interrupts the recovery across the clearing.

performances.physicalActionRelationship: Voice deliberately contradicts then confirms the body: he sounds ready, but the sneeze proves his body is still sneeze-disrupted.
performances.expectedTiming: Answer quickly after Aida’s invitation, within about 0.3s. Sneeze overtakes almost immediately after “Aida!”

performances.speaker: Aida
performances.voiceIdentity: Aida: steady, affectionate, lightly amused; humor stays tucked under care.
performances.dramaticIntention: Aida wants to steady Keen after the sneeze and keep him moving toward her without embarrassment.
performances.subtext: Yes, I saw that too. You’re safe, and we’ll handle it together.
performances.relationshipTarget: Keen, now more clearly present across the clearing.
performances.emotionalEntry: Already oriented toward him, amused by the second interruption but not derailed.
performances.emotionalExit: Settled caretaker energy; the opened path is ready for them to move together.
performances.pace: Short and gentle; no rush, no punchline shove.
performances.rhythm: A small caretaking button: blessing first, his name as warmth.
performances.pauses: No internal pause; allow a soft half-beat after the line for Keen’s recovery/body business.
performances.breaths: Tiny smile-breath before speaking, almost inaudible.
performances.nonVerbalActions: Aida remains grounded and outward-facing, letting the space stay open rather than stepping back into the ritual.
performances.elevenLabsV3Direction: ElevenLabs text: Bless you Keen. Put the warmth on “Keen,” as if protecting his dignity. Smile is audible but small; do not overplay the joke.
performances.physicalActionRelationship: Voice supports Aida’s stillness: a calm verbal hand on the shoulder while her body stays composed.
performances.expectedTiming: Land after Keen’s sneeze finishes and the comic force has settled, about 0.4s later. Line lasts about 1.2s, then hold outward-facing calm before the cut.

orderedEvents.text: Soft mist floats through tall trees. AIDA sits beside a crystal bowl. She slowly circles a mallet around the rim. A warm tone hums through the clearing. Her ROSE QUARTZ PENDANT begins to glow. Pink light fills her eyes.
VISION – THROUGH AIDA'S EYES
A small red squirrel sits inside a hollow tree. He packs a satchel. Unpacks it. Packs it again. He doesn't move. BACK TO SCENE. Aida gently stops the bowl. She places a paw on her heart.

beats.whatChanges: The clearing’s ordinary morning quiet becomes a rose-lit field of attention, and Bo’s private stop-start packing changes from unseen offscreen life into the scene’s central need.
beats.whoDrives: Aida drives the change by holding still, sounding the bowl, and staying with what the vision shows instead of rushing to interpret it aloud.
beats.audienceAnticipation: The audience leans into the hush, expecting the bowl tone to reveal who needs help and what kind of trouble the day is asking Aida to notice.
beats.actionOrChoice: Aida lets the bowl tone pull the scene into the rose haze; within it, Bo repeatedly packs, hesitates, almost commits, then stalls or undoes the motion. Aida chooses to read the repetition gently, without naming the feeling or turning it into a lesson.
beats.consequence: Bo’s threshold behaviour becomes tenderly unmistakable: he wants to go, but cannot yet cross. The rose haze makes the struggle feel close, private, and fragile rather than like information in a magic object.
beats.emotionalOrComicHandover: The beat hands over a sacred hush with pressure inside it: the audience understands that someone needs help before the scene allows any comic release.

storyIntent.narrativeFunction: Reveal the day’s need through Aida’s rose-lit vision: Bo wants to leave for the Learning Circle but cannot yet cross the threshold.
storyIntent.secondaryAudienceFeeling: A quiet ache of recognition for a child frozen before a new place.
storyIntent.outerAction: Aida sounds the bowl; rose light opens a vision; Bo packs, unpacks, and repacks; Aida stops the bowl and places a paw on her heart.
storyIntent.innerAction: Aida moves from searching carefully to understanding gently that the help must meet Bo at the threshold.
storyIntent.performanceDirection: Aida listens with her whole body by doing almost nothing; Bo’s hands reveal the struggle through repeated action and stalled exit.
storyIntent.mutedRead: With no sound, the audience sees ritual attention become a rose vision, sees Bo’s repeated satchel loop, and sees Aida receive it as concern rather than alarm.
storyIntent.environmentPressure: The clearing behaves like a listening circle where mist, dew, and bowl vibration make every small movement matter.
storyIntent.soundStory: The G-rooted bowl tone opens and sustains the rose field; it carries attention rather than explaining feeling.
storyIntent.motifUse: The calm bowl-circle notices the half-finished packing motif; Bo’s satchel and doorway become the visible sign of almost-ready but not yet able.

storyIntent.mustUnderstand: Bo wants to go but cannot yet move out of the hollow tree, and Aida understands this without naming it aloud.
storyIntent.mustNotKnowYet: The audience must not yet be told that Keen’s messiness is the method of help; that turn belongs to the sneeze rupture.
storyIntent.reactionBeat: Aida’s paw-to-heart is the meaning-changing reaction: she holds Bo’s stuckness with care instead of solving it in the vision.
storyIntent.relationshipDistance: Aida and Bo are physically separate but emotionally close through the vision.
storyIntent.relationshipPowerDynamic: Aida has the calm capacity to notice, but she does not dominate or fix Bo’s private moment.
storyIntent.touchOrAvoidance: No direct touch across the vision; Aida’s only touch is to her own heart, keeping the response respectful.
storyIntent.eyelineRule: Aida’s eyeline follows the bowl into the rose field, then returns inward as she stops the bowl.
storyIntent.silhouetteRead: A still seated figure, a circular bowl, then a small figure held inside a doorway with a satchel moving but feet not crossing.
storyIntent.silenceRule: Protect silence after the vision releases; do not fill Aida’s recognition with extra business.
storyIntent.scoreInstruction: Let the bowl tone be the score; no added melodic lift until after the vision has returned to morning air.

shots.physicalPerformance: Aida’s body stays rooted beside the bowl, with only the slow mallet circle, a quiet breath, and softened eyes carrying the ritual. Inside the rose field, Bo’s paws repeat the satchel task in a stop-start rhythm: commitment gathers, stalls, reverses, then gathers again without his feet crossing the hollow-tree threshold. On return, Aida lets the bowl quiet and brings one paw to her heart, receiving the vision without extra motion.
shots.animationTiming: Unhurried restraint. Let the bowl action breathe, give Bo’s repetition enough pauses to become readable, then hold Aida’s paw-to-heart recognition softly before the cut.

performanceContract.playableIntention: Aida is not trying to command an answer; she is making the clearing safe enough for the need to show itself. Bo is caught in an almost-ready loop that his hands reveal before any explanation could.

phases.observableAction: Aida sits grounded at bowl height and circles the mallet around the rim with an even, restrained hand as rose light gathers along the bowl and in her eyes.
Bo packs the satchel, stops before leaving the hollow-tree opening, unpacks it, then packs it again while remaining inside the threshold.
Aida gently stops the bowl, lets her gaze soften after the vision releases, and places one paw against her heart.
The full-frame rose haze thins back into warm morning air while the bowl surface and surrounding mist become still.

performanceContract.physicalCauseAndEffect: Aida’s steady mallet pressure keeps the bowl vibrating; the vibration draws rose light into the frame and opens the vision. Bo’s repeated handling changes the satchel’s state without changing his position, making the unstepped doorway the visible obstacle. When Aida removes the mallet’s motion, the tone and rose field subside, leaving her paw-to-heart gesture as the physical receipt of what she has seen.
performanceContract.visibleEmotionalTurn: The shot changes from ceremonial listening to tender recognition: Aida’s eyes move from searching focus to softened concern, and Bo’s repeated packing becomes the evidence she holds.
performanceContract.requiredLanding: End on Aida beside the quiet bowl with one paw at her heart, rose glow fading into morning warmth, clearly understanding that Bo is stuck at a threshold without having fixed it.
performanceContract.performanceFreedom: Keep the exact cadence of Bo’s pauses, Aida’s breath, robe follow-through, and rose-haze dissipation flexible, as long as the actions remain restrained, readable, and never rushed.

showrunnerJudgement: PASS. I tried to break this and it holds. The scene preserves the selected experience: Aida’s sacred hush is not treated as generic mystical coverage, Bo’s private stop-start packing is the emotional evidence, and Keen’s sneeze arrives as a bodily comic rupture that changes the kind of help being offered. The strongest choice is keeping Keen off-camera at the first sneeze so Aida’s absorption of the interruption, not a cutaway gag reveal, carries the turn. The costly choice is visible enough: Aida does not reseal the ritual; she opens the circle toward Keen and turns solemn noticing into friend-shaped action.
treatmentComparison: The storyboard remains close to the treatment’s central promise. It begins with the bowl as an active listening centre, lets the rose vision fill the frame rather than sit as a decorative magic object, compresses around Bo’s threshold behaviour, then returns depth to the clearing when Keen’s sneeze breaks the spell. Aida owns the point of view throughout: her stillness frames Bo’s stuckness, and her outward turn reframes Keen’s mess as useful companionship. The muted/silhouette legibility test is satisfied by Bo’s repeated packing at the hollow-tree threshold; the audience can understand his almost-ready feeling without dialogue. The sneeze is not random noise because the staging makes it alter Aida’s orientation and the scene’s mission.
packingJudgement: PACKING PASSES. The split is acceptable because the combined adjacent units are planned at 37 seconds, over the 30-second Seedance ceiling. This is not an avoidable join under the stated packing rule. The boundary also protects a real state change: full-frame rose vision/Aida recognition into sneeze rupture/opened clearing. Both units are short, but neither reads as empty padding given the required hush, Bo repetition, exact dialogue, off-camera sneeze timing, Aida’s choice, Keen’s answer, and final blessing.
